n: In this lecture we study the synthetic phenylalkylamines: amphetamine, methamphetamine, the methoxy and methylenedioxy derivatives, their narcological significance and analysis. The outline is as follows: classification, properties, action, “ecstasy” tablets, the Marquis reaction, TLC, UV spectra, precursors and lethal concentrations. Key terms: amphetamine, methamphetamine, MDA, MDMA, DOM/STP, Marquis reagent, Rf and UV maximum.

Synthetic phenylalkylamines are divided into four groups. The first is amphetamine, the main representative. The second is methamphetamine, that is, the N-methyl derivative. The third is the methoxy derivatives, in which the hydrogen of the benzene ring is substituted. The fourth is the methylenedioxy derivatives, which form a separate group: MDA, MDMA and others.

Let us memorise the synthesis dates in sequence. MDA was first synthesised in 1910, MDMA in 1914, methamphetamine in 1919. DOM/STP was synthesised in 1963 by the chemist Alexander Shulgin and appeared in the USA in 1967. MDEA, that is, N-ethyl-MDA, was synthesised in 1980.

Physical properties of amphetamine. Amphetamine is a colourless, volatile, oily liquid with a characteristic odour reminiscent of fish. It is poorly soluble in water and readily soluble in organic solvents. Its boiling point is 200-203 °C. Remember: amphetamine is a liquid.

t: Isomers of amphetamine and their action
n: Amphetamine has two isomers: dextroamphetamine, which rotates polarised light to the right, and levoamphetamine, which rotates it to the left. The dextrorotatory isomer acts on the central nervous system 3-4 times more strongly. Amphetamine enhances the production of neurotransmitters that stimulate the central nervous system, that is, dopamine and noradrenaline.

Amphetamine causes strong psychological dependence and tolerance; dose escalation or adverse states are always observed. It has a strong toxic effect on the human body. In chronic poisoning there are chronic fatigue, insomnia, low mood and weight loss. Gastrointestinal disturbances, tachycardia, hypertension and arrhythmia are also observed.
There are four pharmacological effects of phenylalkylamines. They stimulate the central nervous system. They have a hallucinogenic effect. They dilate the bronchi. They suppress appetite.

Let us compare amphetamine and methamphetamine. Amphetamine is an oily liquid with a boiling point of 200-203 °C, poorly soluble in water. Methamphetamine, by contrast, is a white powder with a bitter taste. The methyl group of methamphetamine increases solubility, so its action on the brain is faster and longer lasting. Both have a stimulating effect on the central nervous system.

Methamphetamine is d-N-methylamphetamine, a white, bitter-tasting, odourless powder. The methyl group attached to the amphetamine molecule enhances the effect. Its solubility is high, and its action on the brain is faster and longer lasting. As a narcotic drug it is taken intravenously, intramuscularly, and also orally and by smoking.

Methamphetamine hydrochloride powder, on standing, forms large crystals and is distributed under the name “Ice” or “Glass”. It was first synthesised in 1919 from ephedrine, red phosphorus and hydroiodic acid, yielding the d-isomer. In the list of precursors, ephedrine, pseudoephedrine and red phosphorus are indicated for pervitin, that is, methamphetamine.

Let us compare the methylenedioxy derivatives. MDA at a dose of less than 80 mg is stimulating, at 150 mg it causes hallucinations, and above 500 mg it is lethal. A single dose of MDMA is 100 mg; the action begins after 30-60 minutes and lasts 4-6 hours. MDEA, that is, N-ethyl-MDA, also causes strong hallucinations.

MDA, that is, methylenedioxyamphetamine, was synthesised in 1910. At a dose of less than 80 mg it has a stimulating effect. At a high dose, 150 mg, it causes hallucinations, and above 500 mg is considered lethal. Tablets are used as the narcotic drug, and one tablet contains 200-230 mg of MDA.

MDMA was first synthesised in 1914; when taken, it enhances perception. A single dose is 100 mg, and the action begins after 30-60 minutes and lasts 4-6 hours. In the 1970s it was produced as 50-100 mg tablets, capsules and powder. N-ethyl-MDA, that is, MDEA, was synthesised in 1980, and it too causes strong hallucinations.

The chemical name of DOM/STP is 2,5-dimethoxy-4-methylamphetamine. It appeared in the USA in 1967, having been synthesised by Alexander Shulgin in 1963. On the black market it was distributed under the designation STP: Serenity, Tranquility, Peace. It is a crystalline substance with a melting point of 60-61 °C.

Let us compare potency. The dextrorotatory isomer of amphetamine acts on the central nervous system 3-4 times more strongly. DOM/STP is 80-100 times stronger than mescaline but 50-60 times weaker than LSD. Its analogues, that is, DOB, DOS and DOI, are somewhat more active.

We get acquainted with the analogues of DOM/STP. DOM/STP is 2,5-dimethoxy-4-methylamphetamine; STP stands for Serenity, Tranquility, Peace. DOB is 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyamphetamine, DOI is 4-iodo-2,5-dimethoxyamphetamine, and DOS is known as “Doctor”. These drugs occur as tablets, powder, capsules and solution.

t: Action of DOM/STP and its analogues
n: DOM/STP is a hallucinogen, 80-100 times stronger than mescaline and 50-60 times weaker than LSD. It is on Schedule I of narcotic drugs. With increased dose, memory loss, brutalisation and depression arise. Its analogues are DOB, DOS and DOI, whose activity is somewhat higher.

The composition of “ecstasy” tablets varies. Tablets are also produced that contain heroin, phentermine and flunitrazepam together with amphetamine. In the tablets, caffeine, aspirin, paracetamol, alpha-methylbenzylamine, ephedrine, quinine, isosafrole, lidocaine, testosterone and chloramphenicol are often found. In some forms, paper sheets impregnated with a solution of the narcotic drug are also distributed.

Preliminary examination of physical evidence. A 5-10 mg tablet is ground, and when 2-3 drops of Marquis reagent are added, a colour appears. Paper containing DOB, DOX or DOM is cut into 1x1 cm pieces, and 1 ml of chloroform and 1 drop of 0.1 M KOH are added. It is boiled on a water bath, the organic layer is evaporated, and 2-3 drops of Marquis reagent are added to the residue.
Colours with Marquis reagent, first part. MDA, MDMA, MDEA, MBDB and BDB give a bluish-black, that is, green-black colour with Marquis reagent. DOM/STP forms yellow, and PMA light grey.
Colours with Marquis reagent, second part. DMA gives a yellowish-green and brown colour. TMA and mescaline give an orange colour. DOB forms emerald green, and DOX yellowish-green.
Colours with Marquis reagent, third part. DOET forms light brown with Marquis reagent, then green. Methamphetamine, by contrast, gives a brown colour.

The TLC conditions are as follows. System: chloroform-acetone-ethanol-25% ammonia solution in the ratio 20:3:1:20; Merck and Sorbfil plates. The table gives, for each substance, the Rf and Rs values and the zone colours with Marquis reagent and ninhydrin. With ninhydrin, MDMA, MBDB, mescaline and methamphetamine give violet, DOB orange, and MDEA an indefinite colour.

TLC results, MDA group. On the Merck plate MDA Rf=0.44, MDMA 0.12, MDEA 0.27, DOM/STP 0.30. On the Sorbfil plate MDA 0.66, MDMA 0.23, MDEA 0.46, DOM/STP 0.46. With ninhydrin MDA gives yellow, MDMA violet, MDEA indefinite, DOM/STP yellow.

t: TLC results (2): PMA, DMA, TMA, DOB
n: TLC results, PMA, DMA, TMA and DOB. On the Merck plate PMA Rf=0.43, DMA 0.38, TMA 0.30, DOB 0.34. On the Sorbfil plate PMA 0.64, DMA 0.54, TMA 0.43, DOB 0.41. With ninhydrin PMA, DMA and TMA give yellow, and DOB orange.

t: TLC results (3): DOX, MBDB, BDB, DOET
n: TLC results, DOX, MBDB, BDB and DOET. On the Merck plate DOX Rf=0.44, MBDB 0.26, BDB 0.60, DOET 0.36. On the Sorbfil plate DOX 0.60, MBDB 0.41, BDB 0.74, DOET 0.52. With ninhydrin MBDB gives violet, the others yellow.

Table 12 gives Rs values together with Rf. For methamphetamine Rs=1.00 on both plates. For MDA Rs is 1.76 on the Merck plate and 1.73 on Sorbfil; for DOM/STP 1.20 and 1.20. The highest Rs is for BDB, 2.40 and 1.95, and the lowest for MDMA, 0.48 and 0.60.

Two more substances appear in TLC as follows. Mescaline on the Merck plate has Rf=0.36, on Sorbfil 0.50, and gives violet with ninhydrin. Methamphetamine on the Merck plate has Rf=0.25, on Sorbfil 0.38, and also gives violet with ninhydrin.

UV absorption spectra are recorded in 0.1 M HCl. Amphetamine, methamphetamine, methylephedrine, norpseudoephedrine and ephedrine give maxima at 251, 257 and 263 nm. Norephedrine gives maxima at 251, 257 and 262 nm. Ephedrone, by contrast, gives a maximum only at 251 nm.

We review the UV maxima by group. Amphetamine, methamphetamine, ephedrine and norpseudoephedrine give maxima at 251, 257, 263 nm; ephedrone only at 251 nm. In the methylenedioxy group, MDA and MDMA give maxima at 235 and 286 nm, and N-ethyl-MDA and MBDB at 234 and 286 nm. Single maxima: PMA 274, DOB 295, mescaline 268, STP, that is, DOM, 289 nm.

UV spectra of the methylenedioxy and other derivatives. MDA and MDMA give maxima at 235 and 286 nm, and N-ethyl-MDA and MBDB at 234 and 286 nm. PMA gives a maximum at 274 nm, DOB at 295 nm, mescaline at 268 nm, and STP, that is, DOM, at 289 nm. These values help to distinguish the substances from one another.

Isolation and analytical methods. Extraction with an organic solvent is carried out under strongly alkaline conditions: with ether, toluene or chloroform. For clean-up, solid-phase extraction, that is, C-18 and XAD-2, and re-extraction are used. For analysis, immunochemistry, thin-layer chromatography and GC-MS, that is, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, are used.

Precursors are the raw materials for amphetamines. 1-phenyl-2-propanone is indicated as the precursor for amphetamine, and 3,4-methylenedioxyphenyl-2-propanone for MDA and MDMA. Isosafrole is for methylenedioxyamphetamine, safrole for MDEA, phenylacetic acid for MDA and its derivatives. Piperonal is listed for amphetamine derivatives, and red phosphorus and pseudoephedrine for pervitin.

We review the lethal concentrations. In death from amphetamine the mean in blood is 8.6 mg/l, range 0.5-41; in liver 30, range 4.3-74; in urine 237, range 25-700. In fatal poisoning with methamphetamine, blood 2.0, liver 4.8, urine 28. The amphetamine metabolite in blood is 0.3.

Detection in urine and cut-offs. Methamphetamine appears in urine 4-6 hours after intake and is detected for 48-72 hours. For amphetamine the cut-off in urine screening is 1000 ng/ml, and in confirmation 500 ng/ml. For methamphetamine the screening cut-off is 1000 ng/ml.

The analytical procedure consists of two stages. In the preliminary stage, a 5-10 mg tablet is ground and a colour is obtained with 2-3 drops of Marquis reagent. In confirmation, identification is carried out by TLC, ratio 20:3:1:20, by Rf and also by the Marquis and ninhydrin colours. The UV spectrum is compared with the maxima in 0.1 M HCl.

We consider practical cases. Case 1: an unknown crystalline powder found on 25-year-old “X” has been brought for forensic chemical examination; carry out a preliminary analysis. Case 2: the child is constantly tired and has insomnia, does not come home at night and is in night clubs; urine and blood samples are analysed. For each case, a table is completed: type of problem, causes of origin and ways of resolution.

To conclude. Amphetamine is an oily liquid with a boiling point of 200-203 °C; methamphetamine is a powder, also distributed under the name “Ice”; MDA and MDMA are methylenedioxy derivatives. The preliminary analysis is carried out with Marquis reagent, and confirmation is done by TLC, ratio 20:3:1:20, UV spectrum and ninhydrin. Review questions: what phenylalkylamines are; narcological significance; reactions and physico-chemical methods of detection; methylenedioxy derivatives.
